# checkmk_downtimes (Data Source)

Lists downtimes currently active on a host, covering both host-level and
service-level downtimes. Useful for detecting downtimes scheduled outside Terraform (in the
CheckMK UI, by another automation, or by `checkmk_downtime` resources managed elsewhere).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    checkmk = {
      source = "withakedo/checkmk"
    }
  }
}

provider "checkmk" {
  url      = "http://localhost:5000/test"
  username = "automation"
  password = "your-secret-here"
}

# List all active downtimes (host and service) on a host, e.g. to detect
# downtimes scheduled outside Terraform.
data "checkmk_downtimes" "web" {
  host_name = "web-01.example.com"
}

output "active_downtime_count" {
  value = length(data.checkmk_downtimes.web.downtimes)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host_name` (String) The host to list downtimes for.

### Read-Only

- `downtimes` (Attributes List) The active downtimes found for this host. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--downtimes))
- `id` (String) Same as `host_name`.

<a id="nestedatt--downtimes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `downtimes`

Read-Only:

- `author` (String) Who scheduled the downtime.
- `comment` (String) The downtime's comment.
- `end_time` (String) End time (RFC3339).
- `id` (String) CheckMK's internal id for the downtime.
- `is_service` (Boolean) True if this is a service downtime, false if it's a host downtime.
- `mode_duration_minutes` (Number) For `flexible` mode, the duration in minutes.
- `mode_type` (String) `fixed` or `flexible`.
- `recurring` (Boolean) Whether the downtime is time-repetitive.
- `service_description` (String) The service name, if `is_service` is true.
- `site_id` (String) The site id of the downtime.
- `start_time` (String) Start time (RFC3339).
